data.name: Shravani
data.gender_notes: Shravani is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Goddess of knowledge, education, and wisdom. She is believed to bring an abundance of knowledge and prosperity to those who invoke her. The name Shravani carries the meaning “Abundance of Knowledge” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit. Parents who choose Shravani usually hope their child will grow to embody abundance of knowledge and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the flow of knowledge and wisdom from the divine to the individual.
data.etymology: Shravani belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Abundance of Knowledge.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Shravani total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

data.cultural_impact: The name Shravani is derived from the Sanskrit word "shravana," which translates to hearing or listening. In Hindu culture, the month of Shravana (July–August) is known as the month of listening to sacred texts and reciting mantras. It is also a month dedicated to the worship of Lord Shiva and Goddess Parvati.
data.spiritual_significance: Goddess Shravani, also known as Saraswati, is the embodiment of knowledge, learning, and wisdom. She is believed to bestow the power of knowledge upon her devotees, helping them to gain insight and understanding. The invocation of her name is believed to aid in the pursuit of knowledge, creativity, and self-improvement.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Shravani signifies the eager and receptive mind, always thirsting for knowledge and wisdom from the divine. It is the embodiment of dedicated listening, believing and following the teachings of the guru and the sacred scriptures.

historical_references.reference: The Hindu goddess Shravani is an aspect of the goddess Parvati, also known as Saraswati during the Shukla Paksha (waxing phase) of the month of Shravana (July–August).

Another belief is that Shravani is the goddess of water, especially the water in the sacred tanks and reservoirs, and she is also known as Haudhini Mata. During the Shravani month, Hindu devotees bathe in these sacred waters and offer prayers to Shravani to seek her blessings.
historical_references.context: Goddess of water, especially in sacred tanks and reservoirs

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Shravani' is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Shravan', which means 'to hear' or 'listening'. During the Hindu festival season, the name 'Shravani' is associated with the Hindu month of Shravana, which is celebrated with various rituals and traditions. On Instagram, you can find numerous posts showcasing the decoration of homes, temples, and the worship of Lord Shiva and Goddess Parvati during this month. On YouTube, devotional music and poetry dedicated to these deities are popular. Lastly, during this period, Google search data indicates an increase in queries related to the significance of the Shravani month, its rituals, and its connection to Hindu mythology.
